event.summary: Check old-terminal shutdown proof before treating tmux clone claims as abandoned
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: startup could discard protection for a working clone checkout if an old terminal can remain alive after migration shutdown. Source basis: assigned patch 00923-001.patch lines 650–670 changes the old-kind branch of spare_claims_at_startup to TerminalKind::Tmux => false because startup ended old terminals; lines 297–314 call OldTerminals::end_private_server without a Result propagation. This is an investigation lead, not a finding. Need to check end_private_server failure contract, reload conversion and clone sweep ownership rules before concluding anything. Suggested bucket: potentially highest (user-owned working checkout loss) only if a surviving old terminal and destructive sweep route are established; otherwise other/unresolved. Confidence: unverified, investigation pending. Could-be-highest: yes. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not searched. No execution or reproduction performed. Exact missing premise: whether failed old-terminal teardown can still reach this unconditional abandoned classification and whether the sweep can remove a live checkout.

event.summary: Failed old-terminal teardown leaves an unprotected spare claim; proposed drop under explicit migration policy
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: if migration cannot end an old terminal or its clone process, startup can remove the private spare it is still updating, so that already-ended launch cannot continue successfully. Original suspected consequence was loss of a working checkout; the available source does not establish that consequence. Details: core.rs:7822–7866 unconditionally classifies a stored tmux terminal as not live; core.rs:8065–8070 passes that snapshot to repo_cache::sweep. spare_checkouts.rs:542–556 removes generated claim directories unless the snapshot protects the session/generation. old_terminals.rs:162–168 and :176–200 deliberately return after teardown failures; module docs :67–78 confirm failures do not stop startup. A spare take has no cache lock (SPEC_impl.md:3983–3986), so the cache sweep lock does not exclude an ongoing take. Source establishes a route to deleting the old launch's private claimed spare if old-process teardown fails, not execution-observed behavior. Could-be-highest: the initial working-checkout-loss hypothesis was considered, but source and contracts restrict the removal to private spare content; actual allocated checkout content is moved out before post-clone commands and the agent run (SPEC_impl.md:4009–4020). No route to deleting the allocated checkout or ordinary user work is established. Suggested bucket: other under the migration's explicit treatment of these sessions as ended; at most high if continuing an unsuccessfully stopped old clone is supposed to be supported. Confidence: confirmed source route, proposed policy drop. proposed_drop: SPEC.md, Terminal experience, lines 3014–3018 (pinned revision): 'A failure to end the server or to stop what ran there is logged and never stops the supervisor from starting; those sessions are treated as ended all the same, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running.' SPEC.md, Managed checkouts, lines 1753–1755: 'Nothing under `.farhelm-spares` that Farhelm did not put there is protected: a spare or building folder there that was removed and recreated, or otherwise replaced, is out of band, and Farhelm may adopt it and delete it'. Independent check should confirm that the explicit old-session-ended policy also permits cleanup of a surviving old clone claim; the general live-claim retention text at SPEC_impl.md:3965–3969 is broader and could otherwise suggest preserving it. possible_cover: none; prohibited coverage sources not searched. Checks made: pinned old-terminal shutdown contract, exact spare liveness branch, startup sweep caller, confined private-name deletion, and complete owned-checkout contracts. No runtime tests or reproductions. Material caveat: this is a teardown-failure residual during the intentional old-terminal migration, not normal terminal-host recovery.

event.summary: Reopened policy check: live legitimate spare claims are not covered by the replacement exception
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: startup can expose a still-running old launch's private spare claim to removal after failed migration teardown; whether this violates the specific live-claim-retention promise remains unresolved. Original suspected consequence: deleting user-owned work in an allocated checkout. Prior narrowing: source establishes private claimed-spare removal but no allocated-checkout deletion route. This synthesis corrects the proposed-drop rationale: SPEC.md:1753–1755 only puts content Farhelm did not put there, or replaced/out-of-band folders, outside protection. It does not itself authorize deleting a legitimate still-running claim. SPEC.md:1748–1752 and SPEC_impl.md:3965–3969 specifically retain live clone claims and uncertain liveness; SPEC.md:3014–3016 and SPEC_impl.md:2922–2927 treat old sessions as ended even when migration teardown fails. Need determine whether the latter is an exception to the former, and establish source confinement of deletion versus moving content into the allocated checkout. Parent reports g109/g112 support accepted surviving-old-agent fallback, not spare cleanup specifically; no parent drop was accepted. Suggested bucket: other or high for interrupted clone preparation under the established route; highest only if allocated/user-owned work loss is established. Could-be-highest: original work-loss hypothesis is preserved and will be checked through actual move/identity ordering. Confidence: confirmed source route to unprotected legitimate claim, policy interpretation unverified after prior investigation. proposed_drop: withdrawn pending reconciliation; the replacement exception is not a sufficient basis. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Next checks: actual take's opened handles, destination validation, no-replace move ordering, confined remover, preparation/agent phase ordering, and independent attachment/retry call chains. No runtime execution or reproductions.

event.summary: Opened removal handles may follow claimed subdirectories into the allocated checkout
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. New synthesis evidence invalidates a blanket confinement claim: spare_checkouts.rs:611–618 parks and verifies the claim root, then checkout_trash.rs:320–349 retains opened child-directory handles on a traversal stack. Concurrent spare_take.rs:156–174 moves entries from its already-open candidate.directory into its already-open allocated destination. A remover that opened a child before its rename can keep traversing that same child after the take moves it into the allocated checkout; the final name/identity check at checkout_trash.rs:374–380 runs after recursive child deletion. This is an unresolved source interleaving, not an executed bug. The initial suspected consequence of deleting user-owned allocated-checkout work must therefore remain live until phase/caller analysis settles it. Existing confirmed consequence remains removal of a legitimate still-running old clone's claim after failed migration teardown. Missing premise: does the take's final unlink of the original claim name (spare_take.rs:176–181) always fail after cleanup parks it, thereby preventing hook/agent work before any affected traversal completes; and can shipped callers allow another session to use the allocated checkout during this interval? Suggested bucket: potentially highest if a route to deleting actual user work is established, otherwise other/high for failed preparation or damaged partial clone. Could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: source-supported interleaving lead; not yet a finding of work loss. proposed_drop: false pending those checks; old-session-ended exception does not by itself settle deletion outside disposable claim contents, and the out-of-band replacement rule is inapplicable to a legitimate claim. possible_cover: none. event.summary: Allocated-checkout work-loss route depends on retained borrowers and predecessor liveness behavior
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. New checks: spare_take.rs:176–181 attempts to remove the claim's original name after moving entries; if startup has parked it under trash, that unlink fails and :181 returns Err before merge, hook or the origin agent. launch.rs:1904–1913 therefore aborts that origin's preparation. This refutes loss of work authored by the origin's own later hook/agent through this interleaving. It does not yet prove confinement to disposable contents: remove_opened_tree_with retains opened children across their move into the destination (:320–349) and validates the final name only after recursive deletion (:374–380). A separate existing host-backed session is permitted to use incomplete allocated contents: core.rs:12202–12217 restricts Ready only for the origin and explicitly permits borrowers; store.rs:3389–3393 admits existing-directory sessions with ancestor memberships rather than preparation. Such a session can survive the update and write moved content while the remover still holds that directory. Original possible work-loss consequence remains potentially highest through this borrower route, while isolated origin preparation damage is narrower. Before concluding a regression, need compare the predecessor's tmux driver after no_server_after_startup: its pane snapshot may already have treated old claims as absent, or may have returned uncertainty protecting every claim. Also verify the relevant older shim used the same handle/move ordering. Suggested bucket: potentially highest if that source route is reachable and attributable; no lowering for rarity. Confidence: source-supported lead; policy exception still ambiguous. proposed_drop: false pending predecessor and historical-shim checks. possible_cover: none. No execution, tests or reproductions.

event.summary: Legacy-claim risk predates the assigned driver-removal patch; blanket confinement remains unproved
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333; predecessor checked: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4. event.summary: Migration can let spare cleanup follow moved directories into a retained checkout
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. Attribution: the same behavior already exists in its immediate predecessor dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4 (the old-terminal migration); the assigned driver-removal patch preserves it. TLDR: after migration fails to stop an old checkout preparation, startup can remove its still-live spare claim. Cleanup can keep traversing a directory after the old shim moves it into the allocated checkout, so work written there by another surviving session can be deleted. This restores the original possible work-loss consequence on a narrower, source-established route; it is not a claim that the allocated checkout root itself is recursively selected by pathname.  Details and exact ordering: (1) core.rs:7843 marks every old-kind row not live regardless of teardown success, and :8065–8070 sends that snapshot to repo_cache::sweep. repo_cache.rs:120–138 takes only the repository cache lock; spare_take.rs:38–40 explicitly takes no such lock, so it does not exclude an ongoing take. Migration agent sweep failures/timeouts are logged and startup continues (old_terminals.rs:306–318, :351–356). (2) A take validates the allocated directory's dev/inode and canonical path, opens the checkout root O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW, then opens the allocated destination and private namespace as separate confined handles (spare_take.rs:295–329, :351–370). Before moving, :142–153 rechecks destination identity and emptiness, enumerates the source and preflights entries; :148–151 orders .git first. The move at :156–174 renames each child from the retained claim directory fd into the retained allocated destination fd, without overwriting. The allocation directory is not replaced. (3) In parallel, spare_checkouts.rs:611–618 opens/verifies the legitimate claim, parks its root under a private trash name, opens/verifies that root and calls remove_opened_tree. checkout_trash.rs:320–349 traverses child directories through retained opened handles. If it opens a child before the take moves that child into the destination, the handle continues to name the moved child. Recursive deletion proceeds through it; the source-name identity check at :374–380 is only after that child's contents were traversed. It can then report that the old source name vanished, but already-deleted content is not restored. No claim-root identity check prevents this movement of descendants out from under an active traversal. (4) Parking the claim makes the take's final unlink of its original claim name fail (spare_take.rs:176–181). That returns an error, so the origin's own merge, configured post-clone command and agent do not run (launch.rs:1904–1913, :1922–1945); this refutes work loss from that origin's later agent/hook. It does not protect an independent existing host-backed session in the allocated directory. Such a borrower is a shipped supported route: an existing-directory create attaches ancestor membership without inheriting preparation (store.rs:3389–3393), and core.rs:12202–12217 explicitly permits borrowers to use incomplete contents while restricting Ready only for the origin. That host-backed session survives migration. It can write new files or Git work into an already-moved child while cleanup still traverses that child, and those writes are ordinary user-owned checkout work, not replacements under .farhelm-spares. A host-backed tab is another possible surviving writer; old_terminals.rs:399–401 skips its launch record during old-tab cleanup. The finding does not require admitting a new client during startup: the borrower can already be running before the update.  Historical/attribution checks: spare_take introduction 1d2ff45e4e5a2de2a6ff9bcc1aac9a9eba647199 predates terminal hosts. Its diff to the reviewed revision changes Git flags, ancestry checking and launch-file enum handling, not the relevant opened handles, .git-first moves or unlink ordering, establishing an older tmux shim with this shape. The predecessor core.rs:6433–6438 already runs migration then unconditionally sets no_server_after_startup. Predecessor tmux.rs:3041–3042 sets presence absent; :2534–2542 and :2983 synthesize NoServer, and :4907–4923 returns an empty pane map. Predecessor core.rs:8173–8188 therefore already omitted protection for old claims. Do not attribute a new regression solely to the assigned :7843 simplification; forward this migration-specific route to the parent for cross-group ownership.  Contract and policy: SPEC.md, Managed checkouts, :1748–1752 says 'Startup removes leftover building and claimed directories except claims still in a live launch’s clone stage' (straight-apostrophe spelling in the pinned source); SPEC_impl.md:3965–3969 retains a still-live NotStarted/clone claim and says failed or uncertain liveness observations retain possible claims. SPEC.md, Terminal experience, :3014–3016 says 'A failure to end the server or to stop what ran there is logged and never stops the supervisor from starting; those sessions are treated as ended all the same, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running.' The isolated legitimate-claim cleanup remains a policy ambiguity: that broad migration-ended rule does not expressly say whether it overrides the specific live-claim retention rule. Source/contracts alone cannot settle that authorial intent; maintainer clarification of that override would settle it. It is not sufficient to cite SPEC.md:1753–1755's replaced/out-of-band-spare rule: this is a legitimate live claim, and borrower writes after movement are outside the private spare namespace. Nor does permission to leave an old process running or start another expressly accept deleting work of a retained host-backed borrower. Parent's g109/g112 reports concern the surviving-old-agent fallback, not this traversal route.  Suggested bucket: highest for the established opened-handle/borrower work-loss route; other/high only for isolated preparation failure when no other session writes moved contents. Could-be-highest: yes; original work-loss hypothesis was narrowed, initially lowered, then restored for this distinct borrower route. Confidence: source-supported concurrency route, not observed execution; the exact scheduling requires cleanup to open a child before movement and a retained writer to act before that traversal ends. Rarity does not lower the consequence. proposed_drop: false for the migration issue; no parent policy drop accepted. The claim that this assigned patch newly introduces it is refuted by predecessor equivalence, which is an attribution correction, not a refutation of the route. possible_cover: parent reports g109/g112 cover accepted old-agent fallback but not spare sweep; no queued findings or excluded metadata searched. No runtime tests, builds or reproductions performed. A fix would preserve uncertain legacy claim protection until cleanup is known safe, or establish exclusion/ownership that prevents a remover following a concurrently moved subtree; the existing namespace and destination identity checks alone do not provide that exclusion.
